To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical current in a multiterminal mesoscopic S-N system depends on the voltage between normal reservoirs in a non-trivial way, that the spin-polarization of the normal reservoirs influences the Josephson effect and that the thermo-emf between normal and superconducting reservoir in such a system is much greater than in the case of ordinary thermoelectricity.

we studied three effects which may be observed in a multiterminal mesoscopic S/N structure: (i) a nonmonotonic dependence of the critical current on the voltage between normal reservoirs, (ii) a dependence of the critical supercurrent on the polarization of electrons in the normal reservoirs; and (iii) an effect of a temperature difference between normal reservoirs on the Josephson voltage.
the Josephson current in the multiterminal structures is a non-monotonous function of the voltage between the normal terminals.
